patient.name: Maria Delgado
patient.chiefComplaint: Continued heavy vaginal bleeding after home delivery 30 minutes ago

history.hpi: Patient delivered a healthy full-term infant at home approximately 30 minutes ago with the assistance of family; no midwife or EMS present for the delivery itself. Placenta delivered spontaneously about 10 minutes after the infant. Family reports steadily worsening vaginal bleeding since placental delivery, soaking through multiple towels. Patient reports feeling increasingly dizzy and weak since the bleeding started.
pastMedical: No prior history of postpartum hemorrhage
history.lastOralIntake: Light snack approximately 6 hours prior to delivery
history.events: Rapid, unplanned home delivery; family called 911 after noting escalating vaginal bleeding following delivery of the placenta

scene.dispatch: 27-year-old female, postpartum bleeding, residence, patient conscious
scene.location: Single-family home, upstairs bedroom, patient supine on bed with newborn wrapped and resting on mother's chest
scene.safety: No hazards to crew; heavily blood-soaked linens on the bed
scene.bystanders: Husband present, assisted with the delivery and called 911; visibly distressed
visualCues: Heavily blood-soaked towels and sheets beneath the patient
Placenta already delivered, contained in a bowl nearby
Newborn wrapped in a towel on mother's chest, pink and vigorous

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 27-year-old female approximately 30 minutes postpartum with a healthy newborn on her chest and ongoing heavy vaginal bleeding soaking through towels. She is alert but reports dizziness and weakness.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, rapid and thready
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact; reports lightheadedness when attempting to sit up
otherFindings: Continued heavy vaginal bleeding with visible clots
Uterine fundus palpable at the umbilicus, boggy and poorly contracted
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy... is the bleeding supposed to be this much?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform fundal massage to promote uterine contraction and control bleeding
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: After delivery, massaging the uterus (should be located at about the umbilicus) and allowing the infant to nurse will promote uterine contraction and help control bleeding
expectedActions.rationale: Uterine atony is the most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage; massage promotes contraction to tamponade bleeding.

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain OB history: prenatal/delivery complications, trauma, anticoagulants, drug use
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Obtain history from patient – history of prenatal or delivery complications, recent trauma, prescription anticoagulants, drug use especially cocaine
expectedActions.rationale: Identifies contributing causes such as coagulopathy or retained tissue that change transport urgency.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access; if unsuccessful within 2 attempts/90 seconds, place IO
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Timely vascular access is essential for fluid resuscitation in ongoing hemorrhage.

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate 500 mL isotonic fluid bolus toward MAP goal 65 mmHg (max 30 mL/kg ≈ 2,040 mL for 68 kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each... Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops.
expectedActions.rationale: Restores circulating volume and perfusion while definitive hemorrhage control (fundal massage) takes effect.

expectedActions.shortAction: Notify medical direction/receiving facility of postpartum hemorrhage
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Notify medical direction/receiving facility if: ... Postpartum hemorrhage
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the receiving facility to prepare blood products and OB resources before arrival.

transitions.if: Fundal massage and IV fluids started
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes a boggy, poorly contracted uterine fundus with heavy ongoing bleeding, performs fundal massage, obtains IV access, and initiates fluid resuscitation.
Crew focuses on IV access and transport logistics without performing fundal massage; the uterus remains boggy and bleeding continues unchecked despite fluids.

phases.name: Fundal massage and IV fluids started
phases.description: Crew performs fundal massage, obtains OB and bleeding history, establishes IV access, and initiates a fluid bolus while continuously reassessing for improvement in bleeding and perfusion.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing the boggy uterine fundus and ongoing hemorrhage, the crew immediately performs fundal massage, obtains OB and bleeding history, establishes IV access per the Shock guideline's two-attempt/90-second threshold, and starts an isotonic fluid bolus toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses stronger but still tachycardic
otherFindings: Fundal massage in progress, uterus beginning to firm

expectedActions.shortAction: Contain placenta and tissue in a plastic bag for hospital evaluation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Contain all tissue in plastic bag and transport
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the receiving facility to assess for retained products of conception.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and estimate total blood loss en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Estimate maternal blood loss. Treat mother for hypovolemia as needed
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment catches recurrent bleeding or delayed decompensation.

transitions.condition: Fundal massage and fluid resuscitation improve uterine tone and hemodynamics; bleeding slows and vitals trend toward normal. Crew packages mother and newborn for transport.

phases.name: Bleeding controlled, transport initiated
phases.description: Fundal massage and fluid resuscitation improve uterine tone; bleeding slows significantly and vital signs trend toward normal. Mother and newborn are packaged together for transport with continued reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: Fundal massage keeps the uterus firm and the fluid bolus restores perfusion; bleeding slows and hemodynamics improve, allowing safe transport.

otherFindings: Bleeding minimal, only light bloody show
Newborn secured to mother per approved neonatal restraint system
Placenta and tissue contained in bag for transport
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot better now, thank you."

phases.name: Fundal massage omitted or delayed
phases.description: Without fundal massage, the uterus remains boggy and atonic. Bleeding continues unchecked, and the patient progresses toward hypovolemic shock despite IV fluids.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew prioritizes IV access and transport preparation without performing fundal massage; the uterus stays boggy and bleeding continues, leading to worsening hypotension and tachycardia despite fluid administration.

clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel like I'm going to pass out..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize hypovolemic shock; perform fundal massage now and escalate fluid boluses toward MAP 65 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each... unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing atony with hemorrhage requires both mechanical (massage) and volume-based rescue.

expectedActions.shortAction: Consider TXA administration per medical direction (MATC does not specify a dose)
expectedActions.rationale: TXA reduces mortality in obstetric hemorrhage when given early, per medical direction.
